enumeration.method: Independent bold-heading enumeration and visual comparison of all four complete Theorems.

checks: All four main-text Theorems are preserved: asymptotic phase and orthogonal results, followed by their finite-sample counterparts. Theorem environments were independently enumerated through the main-text prefix of page 29. The italic no-noise consequences in Theorems 1-2 belong to their original statements.

Nine original entries and twelve supporting passages retain unit-complex and orthogonal parameter spaces, both masked Gaussian models, matrix completions, both spectral estimators, full-rank polar normalization and both source loss definitions.

Independent reconstruction gives 12 direct uses and 18 related connections. Each theorem depends on its own model, estimator and loss. Population eigenvectors/eigenspaces and first-order approximations are proof-only. The phase and orthogonal dependency sets remain disjoint.

The phase estimator returns 1 for zero eigenvector coordinates. The orthogonal estimator returns the identity for singular blocks and invokes the polar map only on full-rank blocks. No invented tie-breaking rule or extension of the polar map is added.

The orthogonal loss display contains a free j and omits the sum suggested by the prose; it is preserved exactly. Other issues include the unit-circle variable typo, zero-noise division convention, complex/real ambient declarations and finite-sample constant scope. Exact theorem remainders and probability constants are retained.

All entries use literal source terms and faithful source-passage/definition headings. Source selectors and explanations are checked for every related theorem. Models and the distinct losses are not merged merely because their roles are analogous.

All six JSON content artifacts reproduce byte for byte from retained per-paper scripts. Source-specific checks and frozen hashes protect the reviewed content; this source census does not certify proofs or silently repair the loss definition.

source_notes.description: The source definition C1={x in C:|z|=1} binds x but uses z in the constraint. The accompanying description says unit complex numbers. Both the printed definition and this contextual interpretation remain separate.

The printed orthogonal loss contains (1/n)||Zhat_j-Z*_j O||_F^2 with a free j and no summation. The text calls it analogous to the summed phase loss and describes stacked matrices, but does not supply a corrected display. The original is preserved and the ambiguity remains explicit.

Theorems 1 and 2 explicitly include sigma=0 consequences, while their preambles and Theorems 3-4 contain np/sigma^2. The author also says the finite-sample result covers no additive noise. No unprinted extended-real division convention is added to the original statements.

The mapping P is displayed on all square matrices but its defining polar formula assumes full rank. Estimator (13) explicitly outputs I_d for singular blocks. That fallback is retained rather than extending the polar factor arbitrarily.

The estimator definitions specify leading eigenvectors/eigenspaces without an explicit tie-selection rule. Main-text unit-vector and orthonormal-column conventions are retained. No deterministic eigensolver or measurable tie-breaking procedure is invented.

The orthogonal-model W is written in a complex ambient matrix space despite real matrix-Gaussian blocks; the Hadamard-product definition also declares a real result for complex inputs. Preserve these source type inconsistencies without discarding imaginary parts or changing the model.

Theorem 3 writes C1,C2,C3>0. Theorem 4 writes C1,C2,C3 without >0 and assumes 2<=d<=C0. The text does not separately spell out every dependence on C0. Original scopes are retained; the bounded-d result is not advertised as uniform over growing d.

The estimator is D3 and phase-aligned averaged loss D4. n,p,sigma retain the model meaning and sequence convention A4. The eigenvector approximations and minimax lower bounds are proof/comparison material, not statement dependencies. Delta=o(1) is existential in the statement; the sigma=0 exact-recovery consequence is part of this Theorem.

ambient_resolution.T2: The real orthogonal model is D6 with group D5, block completion A2 and matrix-Gaussian convention A3. No phase model or first-order perturbation API is imported. Delta=o(1) and the no-noise exact-recovery consequence are stated explicitly.
